items.stem: Which of the following is the correct expansion of the perfect square $(x-5)^{2}$?
items.hint: A squared binomial is a product: rewrite $(x-5)^{2}$ as $(x-5)(x-5)$ before touching anything else.
worked: $(x-5)^{2}$ means $(x-5)(x-5)$; the exponent belongs to the whole bracket, not to each term separately.
Multiply term by term: $x\cdot x=x^{2}$, and $x\cdot(-5)$ together with $(-5)\cdot x$ give $-5x-5x=-10x$.
The last term is $(-5)(-5)=+25$, since a negative times a negative is positive.

items.stem: Exactly one of the four statements below is true. Which one?
items.hint: Multiply each right-hand side back out; only the true statement gives back its left-hand side exactly.
worked: Expand $(x-6)(x+6)$: the middle terms $+6x$ and $-6x$ cancel, leaving $x^{2}-36$, so that statement is true.
$(x+6)^{2}=x^{2}+12x+36$, not $x^{2}+36$; a sum of two squares has no factorization with real coefficients.
$(x-6)^{2}=x^{2}-12x+36$, so the last statement has the wrong sign on the $36$.

items.hint: Ask which power of $x$ gives $x^{6}$ when it is cubed, then recall that every sign inside the second factor of a difference of cubes is a plus.
worked: $x^{6}=(x^{2})^{3}$ because exponents multiply, and $8=2^{3}$, so this is a difference of cubes with $a=x^{2}$ and $b=2$.
Here $a^{2}=x^{4}$, $ab=2x^{2}$ and $b^{2}=4$, and both signs inside the trinomial are $+$.
So $x^{6}-8=(x^{2}-2)(x^{4}+2x^{2}+4)$, and neither factor breaks up further over the integers.
